node: Online learning and workforce retraining demand
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: This node maps most cleanly to public operators monetizing adult learning and workforce retraining, not consumer edtech hype. The clearest exposures are one reference leader, Stride, plus underfollowed mid-cap names tied to employer-sponsored education, online degrees for working adults, and healthcare workforce pipelines. Layer 1B expands the universe around the chokepoint hypothesis that education demand is constrained less by raw content and more by trusted delivery, completion, payments/servicing, credential pathways, and outcome proof. The most relevant scarce-supplier lane is not consumer learning apps, but institutional service providers, student-finance infrastructure, healthcare/workforce program operators, and simulation or delivery infrastructure vendors that universities and employers need to scale regulated or job-linked online programs. Layer 1B expansion for the online learning and workforce retraining demand node. The most relevant public-market candidates are not only consumer-facing learning platforms, but service providers that monetize trusted delivery, licensure pathways, university partnerships, employer education relationships, payments, student servicing, and measurable completion/outcome infrastructure. This pass emphasizes underfollowed small/mid-cap or niche assets; candidates are research leads, not recommendations. The clearest public exposure is not the consumer-facing learning app; it is the hidden plumbing around workforce education: healthcare training, tuition/payment rails, university service providers, and employer-benefits administration
